simple.meaning: פָּסַח (pâçach) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to hop , i.e. (figuratively) skip over (or spare); by implication, to hesitate ; also (literally) to limp , to dance.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Exodus, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, Isaiah, beginning at Exodus 12:13. Its contexts include family line, sacrifice, blood, kingship, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּסַח (H6452).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: פָּסַח (pâçach) / H6452 is traced through Exodus 12:13, Exodus 12:23, Exodus 12:27, 2 Samuel 4:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

timeline.evidenceText: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.

For Yahweh will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, Yahweh will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.
that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of Yahweh’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’ ”

Now Jonathan, Saul’s son, had a son who was lame in his feet. He was five years old when the news came about Saul and Jonathan out of Jezreel; and his nurse picked him up and fled. As she hurried to flee, he fell and became lame. His name was Mephibosheth.

The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here;” thinking, “David can’t come in here.”
Elijah came near to all the people, and said, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If Yahweh is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.”

They took the bull which was given them, and they dressed it, and called on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, “Baal, hear us!” But there was no voice, and nobody answered. They leaped about the altar which was made.
As birds hovering, so Yahweh of Armies will protect Jerusalem.

definitions.full: H6452. pacach I. מָּסַח verb pass or spring over ; — Qal Perfect 3masculine singular ׳פ Exod 12:27 , ׳וּפ consecutive V:23 (J); 1 singular וּפָסַחְתִּ֫י 12:13 (P), all with עַל , of ׳י passing over (sparing) houses of Israel; Infinitive absolute מָּסוֺחַ Isa 31:5 a passing over (SC. עַליְֿרוּשָׁלַםִ ). II. [ מָּסַח ] verb limp (Thes below I. ׳פ but dubious; Arabic is dislocate ; according to Gerber 73 II. ׳פ is denominative from מִּסֵּחַ [and this below I. ׳פ ?]); — Qal Participle plural הַסְּעַמִּים עַלשְֿׁתֵּי מֹּסְחִים 1Kin 18:21 figurative (see [ סְעִמָּה ]). Niph`al Imperfect 3masculine singular וַיִּמָּסֵחַ וַיִּמֹּל 2Sam 4:4 and he fell and was made limping (lame). Pi`el Imperfect 3masculine plural עַלהַֿמִּזְבֵּחַ וַיְפַסְּחוּ 1Kin 18:26 they went limping (along by the altar), i.e. probably in their dance, see Kit Pietschm Phön. 220 (Gr ויפסעו [ = וַיִּפְשְׂעוּ ] stepped ).
